## What about in Julia

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="54%"}
```julia
using CensoredDistributions, Distributions, Turing

@model function double_censored_model(values, weights)
    α ~ truncated(Normal(1, 2), 0, Inf)
    θ ~ truncated(Normal(1, 2), 0, Inf)
    d = double_interval_censored(
        Gamma(α, θ); upper = 15, interval = 1
    )
    values ~ weight(d, weights)
end

model = double_censored_model(values, weights)
chain = sample(model, NUTS(), MCMCThreads(), 1000, 2)
```

::: {.attribution}
Model code from `README.md:71-85`, run for this talk against v0.2.22 ·
[CensoredDistributions.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/CensoredDistributions.jl)
:::
:::
::: {.column width="46%"}
- Changing language here changes the backend. Turing, not Stan
- Each adjustment is a wrapper. `primary_censored` is the $w_P$
  integral, `upper` truncates at $C$, `interval_censored` is $w_S$.
  `double_interval_censored` stacks all three in that order
- The delay is built inside the model from the sampled parameters
- `cdf(primary_censored(Frechet(2, 1), Uniform(0, 1)), 3.0)` returns
  `0.847`. Nobody wrote that method
:::
